items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: Gabler had the Commodore Music Shop, and I ran into Lester

ctx.x: This story about Lester, speaking of the nature of the man. He was very deep and very bright and conserved words as he did notes, to make beautiful sentences, and he -- I had made -- now, let's see.

I had left Goodman and Lester had left Basie just about the same time and I ran into Lester in 52nd Street, Gabler had the Commodore Music Shop, and I ran into Lester and I said, 'Would you come in and hear a Trio album that I just made -- it was the one I made with Jess Stacy and George Wettling and Three Little Words was on the album and so we played it, and Lester said, 'Oh, could I hear that again, and I said, 'Thank you, I am very delighted you like it.'

So we played it all over again and he started singing and whistling phrases from it. Now, I was not to see Lester again until -- let's see, that would have been I think I left Benny, about the end of '38 maybe '39. I hope that is the right year, although I don't think it matters too much.
